business_problem: Condé Nast needed a recommendation engine that could help millions of readers across more than 70 websites find relevant content without the latency, cost, and operational complexity of maintaining separate Elasticsearch pipelines for different asset classes.
solution_summary: Condé Nast consolidated the content assets behind more than 70 websites on MongoDB Atlas so it could rebuild its recommendation engine without maintaining separate Elasticsearch pipelines for each content type. Articles, images, audio, and video are stored centrally, then processed through Voyage AI embedding models to create vectors that are loaded into MongoDB Atlas Vector Search. The recommendation service queries those embeddings directly from Atlas to run image-based and similarity search for 'read more' experiences, while the same managed platform absorbs around 1,500 recommendation queries per second and 500 search queries per second. By moving storage and vector retrieval onto one data platform, the team eliminated brittle external pipelines, reduced operational complexity, and created a stable base for future hybrid search and cross-asset AI experimentation.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores Condé Nast's cross-brand content corpus and supports the managed recommendation infrastructure.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
solution_components.role: Serves vector-based recommendation and similarity queries over millions of content embeddings.

solution_components.name: Voyage AI
solution_components.role: Provides the embedding models Condé Nast uses to generate high-quality vectors for recommendation search.

data_flow: Content from more than 70 Condé Nast websites is centralized in MongoDB Atlas, transformed into embeddings with Voyage AI, stored in MongoDB Atlas Vector Search, and queried by recommendation services that return related content to readers through search and 'read more' experiences.
business_outcome: Condé Nast reduced recommendation latency by 90%, cut operational costs by 65%, raised click-through rates to 35%, and gave engineers a stable platform they can reuse for hybrid search and other AI-driven content experiences.
